scope: Portable descriptive real-HTTP/PostgreSQL work-inbox benchmark harness; no API, domain, authorization, persistence-schema, or SLO changes.

harness.transport: Loopback TCP HTTP to a local FastAPI process with an isolated PostgreSQL 16 Docker container; random container name and Docker-assigned host port.
measurements: Per-request latency samples, p50, nearest-rank p95, sample count, and second-page latency.
API process CPU ticks where /proc is available.
API RSS baseline, sampled peak, final RSS, and peak above baseline via /proc or POSIX ps.
PostgreSQL cgroup CPU delta when the container exposes cgroup v2 cpu.stat.
Source commit, Python version, host platform, and PostgreSQL server version.
correctnessChecks: Exact project-filtered eligible total matches independent fixture authorization enumeration for every timed request and second page.
Page one and its keyset continuation contain the requested number of rows and do not overlap.
A newest same-project row with a forbidden location is denied by the real read guard and never appears in either page; total excludes it.
A foreign actor role assignment sent with the SUP session produces HTTP 403 NOT_AUTHORIZED.
harness.cleanup: Stops the child API process and removes only this invocation's randomized disposable PostgreSQL container.

acceptanceLimits: No latency SLO or p95 budget was found in inspected contracts; results will be descriptive and cannot be called a performance acceptance pass.
Synthetic duplicated Issue records, one API process, and local snapshot persistence do not establish field data, concurrent-client behavior, M4/ARM64 performance, or production readiness.
A product owner must supply the target workload and latency/CPU/memory budgets before field performance acceptance can be claimed.
